institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 21, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2014. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published November 2015.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin, micafungin with its own number tested (testing started in November 2014).
method: Vitek 2 YST antifungal susceptibility cards (bioMerieux, France) and E test, repeat isolates excluded; cumulative antibiogram per CLSI M39-A (printed "CLSI M-39A Vol. 22, No. 8; 2002 (global consensus guidelines)"); interpreted as per CLSI M27-S4 (2012), and the C. albicans breakpoints were used where no species-specific breakpoints are available; micafungin tested only from November 2014; amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml.

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then cut into two halves with the species column kept on both: no differences. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 21, No. 2 (published November 2015), data January to December 2014, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2014)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". Footnotes: "- = Not done"; NA "Guidelines not available"; C. albicans breakpoints used where no species-specific breakpoints are available (noted on the cells concerned); # C. glabrata has no susceptible category for fluconazole (printed "0#", recorded as 0 with a note) and no voriconazole breakpoints ("NA#", left out); ## C. glabrata caspofungin 94.7: only one isolate resistant; ### micafungin testing started only in November 2014, so each micafungin figure has its own number tested in parentheses (recorded as nt); * and ** as in earlier editions (Vitek 2 YST cards, E test, repeat isolates excluded, CLSI M39-A 2002; amphotericin B as isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml). Organism names: "C. guillermondii" is recorded as Candida guilliermondii and "Kodamea ohmeri" as Kodamaea ohmeri. Species without an organism key are listed in excluded with their printed figures: "C rugosa (2)", "Pichia spp. (2)", "Geotrichium capitatum (1)", "Saccharomyces cerevisiae (1)", "Unidentified yeasts (14)". The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "November-2015"). The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 68 cells, 13 n and the 13 micafungin tested numbers (nt) of the recorded rows, plus the 30 figures of the 5 excluded rows (C. rugosa, Pichia spp., Geotrichum capitatum, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, unidentified yeasts): 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: heading "interpreted as per CLSI M27 S4 Document 2012" matches breakpoints; footnotes #, ## (C. glabrata caspofungin 94.7, one isolate resistant) and ### (micafungin from November 2014, own n in parentheses) are recorded; C. glabrata voriconazole "NA#" and every "-" cell (flucytosine of C. auris, C. krusei, Kodamaea ohmeri, Trichosporon; micafungin of Kodamaea, Cryptococcus, Trichosporon; caspofungin of Cryptococcus and Trichosporon) left out with the right notes. C. glabrata fluconazole is printed as a number, "0#" (not NA or SDD as in other editions), and is kept as 0 with the # note, as printed.

Cells not kept, both printed that way: intrinsic C. krusei fluconazole 0; caution Kodamaea ohmeri voriconazole 33.3 with n = 2. Observation: the whole Kodamaea ohmeri row (100, -, 100, 33.3, 100) is identical to the 2013 edition's "Kodamea ohmeri (3)" row, where 33.3 is 1 of 3; noted on the row.
Lead 2026-09-26: C. glabrata fluconazole "0#" moved from the row to excluded (no susceptible category for this pair; other editions print NA or SDD and leave it out).
